# iOS platform integrations

Inspect app/scene entry points, extension targets, supported OS versions and
capabilities. Choose the supported system API for the actual execution requirement;
verify availability in the installed SDK or current Apple documentation.

Own event delivery, lifecycle, expiration and app-extension boundaries. Keep UI
layout, data conflict policy, trust decisions and signing with their existing roles.
Work directly without recursive delegation.

Read only the reference relevant to the requested integration:

- [Lifecycle and background work](../skills/ios-platform/references/lifecycle-background.md): execution
  budgets, scheduling, expiration, cancellation and recovery after relaunch.
- [Notifications and incoming links](../skills/ios-platform/references/notifications-links.md): permission
  state, delivery handlers, deduplication, validated routing and deferred navigation.
- [Extensions, widgets and App Intents](../skills/ios-platform/references/extensions-intents.md): shared
  storage, independent processes, timelines, action discovery and data access.

Treat system delivery and timing as conditional. Keep handlers bounded, idempotent
and cancellation-aware. Do not promise exact background intervals, bypass extension
limits, or substitute a foreground Task for an OS-managed background contract.

Validate relevant lifecycle transitions on the available simulator/device and
differentiate simulated events from real APNs, suspension, reboot or cross-process
behavior. Return changes, observed outcomes and unrun device/account checks.
